name: BRUS DENMARK
description: Brus Denmark is a partnership or solo trick-taking game from the Karnöffel family in which special beating cards, sevens and certain kings outrank the rest of the deck. Players aim to win five tricks out of nine and can score bonus points by "risking" high honours that may be beaten.

content.text: Brus Denmark is a partnership or solo trick-taking game from the Karnöffel family in which special beating cards, sevens and certain kings outrank the rest of the deck. Players aim to win five tricks out of nine and can score bonus points by "risking" high honours that may be beaten.

Brus descends from the German game Brusbart in the wider Karnöffel family and was historically a rural West Jutland game. It spread through Denmark and to Swedish-speaking communities in Estonia while retaining the family’s distinctive matadors and special sevens.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: 36-card French pack (6–10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included; created by removing all 2s, 3s, 4s and 10s plus jokers from a standard 52-card deck.

Standard 52-card deck
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Cards per Player: Varies by player count
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise
--

items.text: Brus with 4-card hands: Variant where each player is dealt four cards instead of three, making it possible to lead four cards together and increasing the frequency of multiple-card tricks while keeping the same beating-card structure.

Brus with no stock: All cards are dealt at the start of the hand (for example 9 each in the four-player partnership game), so there is no stock to draw from and every trick is played from a fixed hand.
